deep.reconstruction:
The page has no formulas. It is a single prose paragraph, written low on an otherwise blank leaf, and it is a draft remark for Riemann's paper on the motion of a homogeneous fluid ellipsoid (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). The many crossed-out attempts on the next page (16) show him working on the same remark.

Setting (my modern gloss). In the Dirichlet-Dedekind-Riemann problem the fluid particle positions are linear in the initial positions, x = M(t) x0. Riemann factors M = T * diag(a,b,c) * S^T, with T and S rotations, a,b,c the semi-axes, and T giving the orientation of the axes of xi, eta, zeta. In modern terms this is the singular value decomposition of M. His differential equations (A) are written in the frame of the principal axes.

Content of the remark, restated:
(i) For an ellipsoid with equal axes, e.g. a = b, the shape of the fluid mass does not fully determine the position of the axes. The ellipsoid is unchanged under any rotation about the third axis, so T (and S) is fixed only up to such a rotation. In SVD language, repeated singular values make the singular vectors non-unique.
(ii) Hence the initial position of the axes generally depends also on the initial motion. Continuity of the motion selects the frame, since the axes must evolve smoothly once a and b separate.
(iii) The position stays genuinely arbitrary ('willkürlich') only when the motion keeps the two axes permanently equal, i.e. a(t) = b(t) for all t.
(iv) Treating this case is easy and needs no further elaboration. But in special cases it can take further particular forms.
(v) Therefore general investigations, such as the general proof that the motion is possible (as done by Dirichlet), would become rather lengthy in Riemann's formulation, because of the many cases needing separate treatment.

My inference, consistent with the next page: the relations from the axes frame back to the fixed frame involve factors like 1/(a^2 - b^2), which degenerate when two axes are equal. This explains why his form of the equations is called less suitable for existence questions, though advantageous for integration and for actually determining the motion.

For context, the next page explains:
- the geometric meaning of real solutions of (A) as direction cosines of the axes with fixed lines (the normal to the invariable plane, and two perpendicular lines lying in that plane);
- that the full position of the axes then follows by a single quadrature.
errors: No mathematical errors; the statement about non-uniqueness of the axis frame for equal axes is correct.

Stylistic or grammatical incompleteness typical of a draft: the clause 'aber in speciellen Fällen noch weitere besondere Formen annehmen' lacks its verb ('kann'), and the subject/verb agreement 'Untersuchungen ... würden' is loose.

results.what: For an ellipsoid with two equal axes, the orientation of the principal axes is not determined by the shape. It depends on the initial motion and is arbitrary only if the axes stay equal for all time. Riemann's axes-frame form of the equations therefore needs separate case treatment, which makes general existence proofs lengthy.
results.modern_name: Non-uniqueness of the singular value decomposition / principal axes at repeated singular values (degenerate case of Riemann ellipsoid equations)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (published remark in his ellipsoid paper); the existence of the motion is due to Dirichlet (1860, edited by Dedekind)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a methodological remark that appears in essentially this form in Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid paper. The content (degenerate principal axes when two axes are equal) is elementary and well known.

checkable.sympy: a,c,th=symbols('a c theta',positive=True); R=Matrix([[cos(th),-sin(th),0],[sin(th),cos(th),0],[0,0,1]]); D=diag(a,a,c); simplify(R*D*R.T - D)
checkable.asserts: Equals the zero matrix: an ellipsoid with two equal axes is invariant under rotation about the third axis, so its shape does not fix the axis orientation.

checkable.sympy: a,c,th=symbols('a c theta',positive=True); R=Matrix([[cos(th),-sin(th),0],[sin(th),cos(th),0],[0,0,1]]); D=diag(a,a,c); simplify((R*D)*(D*R.T)... ) # i.e. simplify(R*D*R.T*R*D*R.T - D**2)
checkable.asserts: Equals the zero matrix: M M^T = D^2 for M = R D R^T, so T is determined by the shape only modulo rotations in the plane of the equal axes.
Vanishes for all theta only when a = b (an off-diagonal entry is proportional to (a-b)*sin(2*theta)), so distinct axes fix the frame and equal axes do not.

transcription_corrections: 'und bleibt nur [-in denen-] unveränderlich' should read 'und bleibt nur [-in denen-] willkürlich'. The page-16 draft confirms this: 'bleibt nur in dem Falle willkürlich'.
'(S. 2 bis dieselbe[?])' is most likely '(z. B. bei Dirichlet)', a reference to Dirichlet's proof of the possibility of the motion.
Interlinear insertion above 'Bewegung' read as 'ursprünglichen'; plausible, and consistent with page 16, 'von der ursprünglichen Bewegung ab'.
'[-denn-] aber in speciellen Fällen' probably intends '[kann] aber in speciellen Fällen noch weitere besondere Formen annehmen'.

'die allgemeinen Untersuchungen [-oder-] z. B.': the 'oder' is struck and 'z. B.' is inserted, followed by the struck 'die Nachweis' and then 'der allgemeine Nachweis'. The current reading is essentially right.
